newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Rangebound Belgian OLOs focus on EMU, data.
newsitem.headline: Rangebound Belgian OLOs focus on EMU, data.

text.p: Rangebound Belgian bonds hovered around unchanged levels on Thursday morning, with traders awaiting U.S. data in the afternoon for inspiration and watching developments in the row over the EMU stability pact.

Nerves at the start of the week after France's new Socialist government insisted the stability pact also focus on jobs have died down and the market has become confident that a deal will be reached in time for next week's Amsterdam summit.
"It's all pure politics - they can't go back (on the single currency timetable) now," one dealer said, adding the only question was how many countries would initially take part.
After meeting European Commission President Jacques Santer on Thursday, French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said his government's concerns on Europe had been understood and progress was being made.

By 0900 GMT the benchmark 10-year OLO was yielding 5.86 percent compared to 5.87 at the previous close, stuck within its recent 5.85-5.95 percent trading range. Its spread over Bunds was unchanged at eight basis points.
Traders said that with thoughts already turning to the Federal Reserve's policy making FOMC meeting at the start of next month more U.S. data this afternoon could boost interest.
U.S. retail sales, due at 1230 GMT, are expected to show a rise of 0.4 percent in May, while weekly jobless claims are forecast at 325,000. Producer price data follows on Friday.

Attention was also focused on the Bundesbank's policy council meeting on Thursday. No rate change is expected, but markets are watching out for any news on talks at the meeting about a controversial revaluation of the bank's currency reserves.
